KUJO 02 / The accountability problem 2 / 18 Software production is outpacing verification. Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision. 01 The claim “Tests passed. Ready to merge.” An illustrative agent statement. 02 The evidence Command, exit code, changed revision, environment and retained failure output. 03 The gap Useful logs already exist. Connecting them across tools and review boundaries remains work. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Thesis · existing agent controls acknowledged 2 2 Software production is outpacing verification.

KUJO 03 / Structural shift 3 / 18 Agents now work across the repository. GitHub documents agents that plan changes, edit code and review pull requests. More delegated work makes the execution record part of the review. 01 More scope Agents move from suggestions to repository tasks. 02 More handoffs The reviewer needs the revision, executed checks and retained failures. 03 Why now Existing platforms establish the workflow; Kujo proposes a portable evidence layer. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing C01 · current GitHub documentation; category context, not Kujo demand 3 3 Agents now work across the repository.

KUJO 04 / Why now 4 / 18 A passing summary can hide a failed checkout. A coupon changes a $50 cart to $50.99 instead of $45. The reviewer needs the failing test, exact change and unchanged checks. 01 Reconstruct Find the task, revision, environment and actual command result. 02 Correct Fix shipping eligibility without weakening the test. 03 Review Compare before and after evidence. Measure buyer investigation time in pilots. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing D01 · controlled checkout regression; buyer cost remains a hypothesis 4 4 A passing summary can hide a failed checkout.

KUJO 05 / The Kujo system 5 / 18 Build with clarity. Operate with control. The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows. 01 Clarity Kujo language / Spec / Eval: explicit intent and testable outcomes. 02 Context MCP / CaseFile / RunLedger: useful inputs, debugging evidence and run records. 03 Control Dispatch / Workcell / ShipCheck: orchestration, bounded execution and release checks. Existing repositories + coding agents explicit component contracts Kujo runtime + CLI Inspect the execution boundary Workcell owns supported container bounds. Dispatch owns workflow state. Neither confers enterprise certification. Inspect the evidence boundary CaseFile captures commands. Eval runs configured checks. RunLedger stores supplied outcomes. Artifacts remain separate. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T01–T14 · tool boundaries remain distinct 5 5 Build with clarity. Operate with control.

KUJO 06 / Lifecycle 6 / 18 Accountability spans the whole task. Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly. 01 Instruction → Context Spec / PackWrite → MCP and repository context 02 Execution → Evaluation Dispatch / Workcell → Eval result artifacts 03 Evidence → Review → Release CaseFile / RunLedger → reviewer → ShipCheck gate Human authority remains explicit at the release decision. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement 6 6 Accountability spans the whole task.

KUJO 07 / Engineering proof 7 / 18 A working foundation precedes this raise. The language, execution tools and integration adapters are inspectable in public source. 01 Language and VM Kujo v1.9.0 release documentation; compiler and VM source pinned for diligence. 02 Workflow tooling CaseFile captures commands. Eval runs checks. Workcell documents bounded execution. 03 Existing entry points Command Code, Hermes, OpenCode and Pi adapters have documented releases and scoped verification. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T01–T14, I01–I04 · documented scope; demo tools rerun locally 7 7 A working foundation precedes this raise.

KUJO 08 / Recorded demonstration 8 / 18 Keep the failure. Verify the correction. A reproducible checkout regression: a coupon must preserve free shipping. The original tests fail, a one-line correction passes them. 01 Before Python test fails: 5099 cents returned instead of 4500. 02 Correction Check the original subtotal for shipping eligibility. 03 After The same three tests pass. CaseFile retains both runs; Eval reruns the gate. Inspect the correction − shipping = 0 if discounted >= 5000 else 599
+ shipping = 0 if subtotal_cents >= 5000 else 599 Open failure, commands & evaluation → Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing D01 · controlled fixture; driver applies correction, no autonomous-repair claim 8 8 Keep the failure. Verify the correction.

KUJO 09 / Adoption without migration 9 / 18 Adopt the ecosystem before the language. Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary. 01 Today: wrap the task Use CaseFile for command evidence and Eval for explicit repository checks. 02 Then: control execution Adopt Dispatch or Workcell after validating the target environment and runtime pins. 03 Over time: go deeper Choose Kujo for new agent tooling where native language integration adds value. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies 9 9 Adopt the ecosystem before the language.

KUJO 10 / Initial customer 10 / 18 Start with the platform engineering lead. Initial buyer hypothesis: a team operating coding agents across repositories and reconstructing failures during review. 01 Purchase trigger An agent regression crosses a review boundary and the team must reconstruct what ran. 02 What we know Local evidence tools work; integration adapters and a public catalog are available. 03 What we are testing Whether shared evidence saves review effort and earns a recurring team budget. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Buyer, demand and willingness to pay remain unvalidated 10 10 Start with the platform engineering lead.

KUJO 11 / Business model 11 / 18 Open tools today. A team service to validate. Primary paid wedge: shared agent-run evidence and review for engineering teams. Application code stays in its existing language. 01 Available now · open source Local CLI tools and documented host integrations; no Kujo subscription required. 02 Planned · team service Proposed $500/month: evidence intake, retention, access controls, review and export. 03 Planned · enterprise Separate $24K/year hypothesis for deployment, policy and support. Excluded from the base case. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing No paid service or active pilot verified; proposed packaging 11 11 Open tools today. A team service to validate.

KUJO 12 / Market model 12 / 18 One team subscription. Explicit revenue milestones. Base pricing hypothesis: $500 per team per month. Customer counts below are scenarios, not forecasts or achieved revenue. $102K ARR · first repeatable revenue milestone 17 teams $1.002M ARR · requires retained paid cohorts 167 teams $6M ARR · long-term sensitivity, not a 24-month promise 1,000 teams Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing FIN01 · ARR = active paying teams × $500 × 12; enterprise excluded 12 12 One team subscription. Explicit revenue milestones.

KUJO 13 / Position and defensibility 13 / 18 Portable evidence across existing workflows. GitHub integrates agents and review. LangGraph persists workflow state. Kujo composes local execution artifacts with explicit evaluation. 01 Demonstrated Before/after command bundles, unchanged checks and an inspectable patch in the checkout demo. 02 Interoperable Existing application languages and documented host adapters; exports stay reviewable outside a chat. 03 To earn A reliable shared service, useful integrations and retained buyer usage. Competitive parity is not a benchmark. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing C01–C04 · documentation comparison; no measured superiority 13 13 Portable evidence across existing workflows.

KUJO 14 / Distribution 14 / 18 Turn a first evidence run into a retained team. Integration-led distribution: one useful repository workflow, then a buyer conversation about shared review. 01 Discover → activate Docs, MCP catalog and host adapters → first captured failure and passing rerun. 02 Validate → pilot Interview 12 buyers; qualify design partners against an actual incident and budget owner. 03 Convert → retain Offer a scoped paid pilot after readiness checks; measure weekly use, review time and renewal. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Proposed 30/60/90-day plan; no completed interviews or pilots claimed 14 14 Turn a first evidence run into a retained team.

KUJO 15 / Momentum 15 / 18 Public engineering and distribution are visible. Technical momentum is independently inspectable. Commercial validation is the next milestone. 01 Engineering Kujo runtime and tools have pinned public source; this deck includes a rerun checkout regression. 02 Distribution Kujolang.ai MCP is listed in the GitHub MCP Registry, observed November 11, 2026. 03 Commercial stage No verified paying customers or revenue in the reviewed evidence. Pilot and retention validation remain ahead. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing E01 · listing is distribution access, not customer adoption 15 15 Public engineering and distribution are visible.

KUJO 16 / Founder and team 16 / 18 A founder with a public shipping record. Robert DeVore builds commercial web software and the Kujo language ecosystem. 01 Independent shipping Public biography describes more than 20 years building software; tenure is self-reported. 02 Third-party adoption WebDevStudios reported adopting his plugins in July 2025. No unsupported plugin count is used. 03 Team to build Stage execution reliability, product design, developer experience and customer development hires. Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing F01–F03 · third-party adoption verified; exact team-leadership scope unverified 16 16 A founder with a public shipping record.

KUJO 17 / Investment and milestones 17 / 18 Fund commercialization with staged commitments. Proposed $6M raise: a 24-month operating plan with $900K reserve. Release hiring against validation, paid pilots and retention. proposed raise · founder confirmation pending $6M proposed post-money SAFE cap · negotiable $30M modeled spend horizon · no revenue offsets 24 mo 0–6 mo Flagship evidence workflow 6–12 mo External validation + pilots 12–24 mo Paid retention + repeatability Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing FIN02 · proposed terms; $30M post-money SAFE cap ≠ a priced valuation 17 17 Fund commercialization with staged commitments.

KUJO 18 / The vision 18 / 18 Discuss the raise. Inspect the evidence. Proposed $6M financing conversation. Start with a technical diligence walkthrough and the team-service thesis. KUJO Trust at the speed of AI. Investor conversations ↗ Evidence & investor appendix ↗ KUJO / Investor briefing Next step: contact Robert through the existing public contact page. Terms subject to agreement. 18 18 Discuss the raise. Inspect the evidence.
